We have seen what ‘the promise of the Father’ involves and how 
it is going to happen. Next, Joel tells us to whom it is going to happen . 
Through Joel, God says: 
I will pour out my Spirit on all people. 
Your sons and daughters will prophesy, 
your old men will dream dreams, 
your young men will see visions. 
Even on my servants, both men and women, 
I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
Joel 2:28–29
Joel is foretelling that the promise will no longer be reserved for 
particular people, at particular times, for particular tasks, but it will 
be for all. God will pour out his Spirit regardless of sex (‘sons and 
daughters… men and women’); regardless of age (‘old men… young 
men’); regardless of background, race, colour or rank (‘even on 
my servants’). There will be a new ability to hear God (‘prophesy… 
dream… see visions’). Joel prophesied that the Spirit would be 
poured out with great generosity on all God’s people. 
Yet all these promises remained unfulfilled for at least 300 years. 
The people waited and waited for the ‘promise of the Father’ to be 
fulfilled until at the coming of Jesus there was a burst of activity of 
the Spirit of God. 
With the birth of Jesus, the trumpet sounds. Almost everyone 
connected with the birth of Jesus was filled with the Spirit of God.
